findings.title: Account for JSON expansion when accepting inventory CSVs
findings.explanation: The UI accepts up to 1 MiB of CSV, then sends all rows as JSON in one request. Repeated metadata property names and JSON syntax can push the request over the existing 1 MiB readAdminJSON limit even when the CSV satisfies every advertised size, row, key, and value limit. Such inventories fail with "request exceeds 1 MiB" and import no rows; retrying the same valid file cannot succeed.
findings.evidence: Executed the new parseInventoryCSV on a 1,000-row CSV with 16 valid 31/32-character metadata keys and 40-character values: parsing succeeded, CSV size was 664,416 bytes, and JSON.stringify({rows}) was 1,273,900 bytes. submitInventory sends that exact serialization at line 660. fleet-manager/src/admin_http.go:280-287 rejects bodies above 1,048,576 bytes. The base already had that HTTP limit; the new CSV upload path introduces the incompatible expansion.
findings.fix: Make the documented CSV limit and import transport agree, for example by applying an appropriately bounded import-specific request limit that accommodates JSON expansion; preserve duplicate-hostname/target checks across the complete inventory. Add coverage for a valid CSV whose JSON encoding exceeds 1 MiB.

Compared base and head tags persistence, admin routes, UI changes, and tests; traced admin authorization, conditional-write retries, organization membership, duplicate-hostname and duplicate-target handling, and metadata validation.
